summary: Ran a UI audit of the translate toggle in all 20 languages. Logged in as merchant 0509999999 and drove the Expo web preview at 390x844 via localStorage token/app_lang. For each language we checked /merchant/products (first 6 names, 2 toggles), /merchant home recent orders (5 names) and /merchant/orders (first 22 names, toggles on #0, #1 and #15 = first Arabic-origin name). No language had a disallowed Latin word in a product or customer name. Latin-script languages had no Arabic or other-script text left. Every toggle shown went translation -> exact merchant/customer original -> back to the same translation. No toast, alert or dialog appeared. All translations showed in about 2-5s. 'NO-TOGGLE' only happens when the shown text is already the original in the viewer's language (English names for Latin languages, pure-Arabic names for ar), which is by design.

minor.issue: Inconsistent across Latin-script languages: 'Samsung Super Fast 45W' is translated only for tr ('Süper Hızlı'). es/fr/de/it/pt/id/ms keep 'Super Fast' in English. Other product names do translate their generic words (e.g. es 'Funda de Cuero para iPhone 15 Pro', 'Cargador MagSafe de Apple').

Names are romanised differently per language (es/de/it/id 'Khalid Al-Shammari' vs fr/en 'Khaled Al-Shammari' vs pt/tr 'Khaled Al-Shamri'). 'HP' is kept in ur/he/ru/ja/ko/hi but transliterated in bn/th/zh. Both are allowed by the rules; this is cosmetic only.

issues: Translatable toggle button is visually about 22x18px (paddingHorizontal 4 / paddingVertical 2), smaller than the TranslatableName one (minHeight 24, padding 6/4). hitSlop 10 lifts the tap area to about 42x38, still a little under 44pt. Suggest copying the TranslatableName iconBtn style.

action_items: Optional: decide whether 'Super Fast' in 'Samsung Super Fast 45W' should be translated for all Latin languages (only tr does it now) and make the rule consistent.
Optional: bring the Translatable (products) toggle size up to match TranslatableName (minHeight 24 + hitSlop 12).
Optional: showToast() does nothing on web, so a failed manual translation gives no feedback in the web preview.
critical_code_review_comments: Translatable.tsx and TranslatableName.tsx repeat about 60 lines (fetchTranslation, the disk cache and the IconBtn render). Consider moving them into a shared hook.

For products, Translatable picks name_en for every non-ar viewer, so the 'original' shown by the toggle is the merchant's English name, not name_ar. This seems intended, but for Latin-language viewers there is never a toggle on product names.

success_rate.backend: N/A (frontend-only request; spot-checked bulk translate for es/de/tr, 0 failures)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (20/20 languages: products, customers and toggles pass)
